title: Our Dead Speak to Us Through the Senses
text:
Our dead speak to us through the senses

while the marsh breathes,

stinks and splashes,

bubbles and flowers,

offers its berries

and carries the bear.


Like the wind passing over the marsh,

lulling the reeds as far as the eye can see,

so our dead are present

under the water,

in the depths of our soul

the drowned plants sway.


Our dead are rooted in us,

they rest in us,

our soul is heavy with drowned branches

and perhaps fruitful,

perhaps in its hollows something forms a chain

and something invisible to us

offers its purpose stealthily,

which

(what a relief!)

is no concern of ours.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Kilpi's marsh ecology as a way of sensing the dead inside the soul.

title: Testament
text:
Having arrived at the time when

twilight no longer consoles me

and small omens diminish me;

having arrived at this

        time;


and since the coffee grounds

now suddenly open for me

        their round bitter mouths;


having arrived at this time;

and having lost already all

        hope of

some deserved promotion, of

seeing the serene flowing of shadow;


and possessing nothing more than this time;

possessing nothing more, in

        the end,

than my memory of the nights and

their enormous vibrant delicacy;


possessing nothing more

between heaven and earth than

my memory,

        than this time;


I decide to make my testament.

It is this:

I leave you

time,

        all the time.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Diego's legal-testament cadence and the final bequest of time itself.
